name: British Army in North America
troop_source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_and_New_Jersey_campaign - "the British transported about 22,000 men, including 9,000 Hessians, from Staten Island to Long Island"

rows.label: Boston (arrives aboard HMS Cerberus)
rows.quote: arrived there aboard HMS Cerberus on 25 May 1775

rows.label: Battle of Bunker Hill
rows.quote: With Howe personally leading the right wing of the attack

rows.label: Boston (takes over as commander-in-chief)
rows.quote: General Gage sailed for England, and Howe took over as Commander-in-Chief
rows.note: Date is Gage's sailing date; Howe stayed in Boston through the winter.

rows.label: Boston (evacuation fleet sails)
rows.quote: On 17 March, British troops and Loyalists evacuated the city, and sailed for Halifax

rows.label: Halifax
rows.quote: On March 30, 1776, General William Howe arrived, having been driven from Boston

rows.label: Staten Island (landing)
rows.quote: Landing unopposed on Staten Island on July 3, 1776, Howe
rows.note: Battle of Long Island article says landings began July 2; 3 July is the date in the campaign article.

rows.label: Battle of Long Island
rows.quote: a large column led by Howe and Clinton passed around the American left flank

rows.label: Kip's Bay landing
rows.quote: On September 15, General Howe landed about 12,000 men on Lower Manhattan

rows.label: Battle of White Plains
rows.quote: Howe remained at Scarsdale until the morning of October 28
rows.note: Source shows Howe with the advancing army that morning; the battle itself is described as his army's action.

rows.label: Battle of Fort Washington
rows.quote: Mathew and his troops, accompanied by Howe, were ferried across the Harlem River

rows.label: Somerset Court House (Millstone)
rows.quote: On June 14, Howe's army marched again toward Somerset Court House
rows.note: Source says Howe remained there five days (to June 19). Present-day Millstone.

rows.label: Perth Amboy
rows.quote: Howe returned to Amboy on June 22

rows.label: Sandy Hook (fleet departs for the Chesapeake)
rows.quote: Howe's army departed from Sandy Hook ... on July 23, 1777
rows.note: Howe article says he 'sailed from New York on 23 July'; same date.

rows.label: Head of Elk (landing)
rows.quote: After landing in Maryland on August 25
rows.note: Other articles say only 'late August'. Head of Elk is present-day Elkton.

rows.label: Battle of Brandywine
rows.quote: The main British column under General Cornwallis (and accompanied by General Howe)

rows.label: Philadelphia (enters the city)
rows.quote: Howe triumphantly entered the city on 26 September

rows.label: Battle of Germantown
rows.quote: Howe rode forward, thinking they were being attacked by foraging or skirmishing parties

rows.label: Philadelphia (army pulls back from Germantown)
rows.quote: On October 19, Howe withdrew the British forces from Germantown
rows.note: Army-level statement; Howe's own movement that day is inferred. Less sure.

rows.label: Philadelphia (departs for England)
rows.quote: On 24 May 1778, Howe left Philadelphia on a ship bound for England
